verses.sanskrit:
वैशंपायन उवाच।
              प्रतिज्ञाय च दुष्यन्ते प्रतियाते शकुन्तलाम्। गर्भं सुषाव वामोरूः कुमारममितौजसम्॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said : When Dushyanta went away from the hermitage, making the (above) promises to Shakuntala, she gave birth to a boy of immeasurable energy. When the child grew only three years old, he became in splendour as blazing as the blazing fire. O Janamejaya, he was endued with great beauty, magnanimity and all accomplishments.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिषु वर्षेषु पूर्णेषु दीप्तानलसमद्युतिम्। रूपौदार्यगुणोपेतं दौष्यन्तिं जनमेजय॥२॥
जातकर्मादिसंस्कारं कण्वः पुण्यवतां वरः। विधिवत्कारयामास वर्धमानस्य धीमतः॥३॥
verses.english: The best of pious men, Kanvas, performed all the rites ordained by the scriptures on that intelligent boy who began to grow up day by day.

verses.sanskrit:
दन्तैः शुक्लैः शिखरिभिः सिंहसंहननो महन्।	
              चक्राङ्कितकरः श्रीमान्महामूर्धा महाबलः॥४॥
verses.english: The boy was gifted with sharp, strong and pearly teeth; he was strong enough to kill lions, he had all auspicious signs on his palms, he had a broad forehead, he was beautiful and strong.

verses.sanskrit: कुमारो देवगर्भाभः स तत्राशु व्यवर्धत। षड्वर्ष  एव बालः स कण्वाश्रमपदं प्रति॥५॥
verses.english: Like a celestial child, he began daily to grow up. When he grew six years old, he was so strong that he seized and bound tigers, boars, buffaloes and elephants to the trees that stood near the hermitage.

verses.sanskrit: सिंहव्याघ्रान्वराहांश्च महिषांश्च गजांस्तथा। बबन्ध वृक्षे बलवानाश्रमस्य समीपतः॥६॥
आरुरोहन्दमांश्चैव क्रीडंश्च परिधावति। ततोऽस्य नाम चक्रुस्ते कण्वाश्रमनिवासिनः॥७॥
verses.english: He rode on some of these wild beasts; he seized some of them and sometimes he pursued some of them in playful mood. The dwellers of the hermitage of Kanva, (finding all this), gave him a name. (They said,) “As he subjugated all beasts, let him be called Sarvadamana". Thus the prince came to be called Sarvadamana, endued as he was with great strength, energy and powers.

verses.sanskrit: अस्त्वयं सर्वदमनः सर्वं हि दमयत्यसौ। स सर्वदमनो नाम कुमारः समपद्यत॥८॥
विक्रमेणौजसा चैव बलेन च समन्वितः। तं कुमारमृषिर्दृष्ट्वा कर्म चास्यातिमानुषम्॥९॥
समयो यौवराज्यायेत्यब्रवीच्च शकुन्तलाम्। तस्य तद्बलमाज्ञाय् कण्वः शिष्यानुवाच ह॥१०॥
verses.english: Seeing the extraordinary acts of the boy, the Rishi (Kanva) told Shakuntala that the time had come when he should be installed as the heir-apparent.
verses.bhavadeepa: विक्रमः पराभिभवसामर्थ्यम् । ओजः कान्तिः बलं शारीरम्  ॥९॥

verses.sanskrit: शकुन्तलामिमां शीघ्रं सहपुत्राभितो गृहात्। भर्तुः प्रापयतागारं सर्वलक्षणपूजिताम्॥११॥
verses.english: Seeing the great strength of the boy, Kanva spoke to his disciples thus, "Take Shakuntala with her son from the hermitage to the house of her husband, blessed with all auspicious signs."

verses.sanskrit: नारीणां चिरवासो हि बान्धवेषु न रोचते। कीर्तिचारित्रधर्मघ्नस्तस्मान्नयत मा चिरम्॥१२॥
verses.english: "It is not fit for women to live for ever in the house of their paternal or maternal relations. Such residence destroys their good name, good conduct and virtue. Therefore, take her to her husband's house without delay."

verses.sanskrit: तथेत्युक्त्वा तु ते सर्वे प्रातिष्ठन्त महौजसः। शकुन्तलां पुरस्कृत्य सपुत्रां गजसाह्वयम्॥१३॥
verses.english: The greatly effulgent disciples (of Kanva), having promised to do it, started with Shakuntala and her son towards the city of Hastinapur.
verses.bhavadeepa: न रोचते न शोभते। चारित्रं शीलम् । धर्मः पातिव्रत्यम् ॥१२॥

verses.sanskrit: गृईत्वाय़्भरगर्भाभं पुत्रं कमललोचनम्। आजगाम ततः सुभूर्दुष्यन्तं विदितद्वनात्॥१४॥
verses.english: That beauty of fair eye-brows, taking her lotus-eyed son of celestial beauty with her, left the forest where she had first met Dushyanta.

verses.sanskrit: अभिसृत्य च राजानं विदिता च प्रवेशिता। सह तेनैव पुत्रेण बालार्कसमतेजसा॥१५॥
verses.english: Having sent words, she entered the royal court with her son, as effulgent as the morning sun. And she was then introduced to him.

verses.sanskrit: निवेदयित्वा ते सर्वे आश्रमं पुनरागताः। पूजयित्वा यथान्यायमब्रवीच्च शकुन्तल॥१६॥
verses.english: The disciples of the Rishi, having told the king everything, returned to the hermitage. And Shakuntala, after duly worshipping the

verses.sanskrit: अयं पुत्रस्त्वया रजन्यौवराज्येऽभिषिच्यताम्। त्वया ह्ययं सुतो राजन्मय्युत्पन्नः सुरोपमः। यथा समयमेतस्मिन्वर्तस्व पुरुषोत्तम॥१७॥
verses.english: Shakuntala said : O King, this is your son. Let him be installed as your heir-apparent. O King, this god-like boy was begotten by you on me. O best of men, fulfil now the promise you made of me.

verses.sanskrit: यथा मत्संगमे पूर्वं यः कृतः समयस्तथा। तं स्मरस्व महाभाग कण्वाश्रमपदं प्रति॥१८॥
verses.english: O illustrious man, call to your mind the agreement you made with me on the occasion of our marriage at the hermitage of Kanva.

verses.sanskrit: सोऽथ श्रुत्वैव तद्वाक्यं तस्या राजा स्मरन्नपि । अब्रवीन्न स्मरामीति कस्य त्वं दुष्टतापसि ॥१९॥
verses.english: Having heard her words, the King remembered everything, but he said, “I remember nothing. O wicked ascetic woman, to whom do you belong?"

verses.sanskrit: धर्मकामार्थसंबन्धं न स्मरामि त्वया सह । प्रच्छ वा तिष्ठ वा कामं यद्वापीच्छसि तत्कुरु॥२०॥
verses.english: "I do not remember to have any connection with you with regard to (either) Dharma, Artha and Kama. Go or stay or do whatever you please."

verses.sanskrit: सैवमुक्ता वरारोहा व्रीडितेव तपखिनी। निःसंज्ञेव च दुःखेन तस्थौ स्थूणेव निश्चला॥२१॥
verses.english: Thus being addressed, the beautiful ascetic lady was filled with shame. She lost her consciousness from grief and she stood like a wooden post.
verses.bhavadeepa: धर्मार्थकामसंबन्धम्। धर्मे चार्थे च कामे च नातिचरितन्या त्वयेयं नातिचरामीति विवाहमन्त्रप्रकाशितं वैवाहिकसंबन्धम्  ॥२०॥

verses.sanskrit: संरम्भामर्षताम्राक्षी स्फुरमाणौष्ठसंपुटा। कटाक्षैर्निर्दहन्तीव तिर्यग्राजानमैक्षत ॥२२॥
verses.english: Soon became her eyes red like copper; her lips began to quiver; she cast upon the king her (angry) glances which seemed to burn him.

verses.sanskrit: आकारं गूहमाना च मन्युना च समीरिता। तपसा संभृतं तेजो धारयामास वै तदा ॥२३॥
verses.english: Her rising anger and blazing fire of her asceticism she kept down with a great effort.

verses.sanskrit: सा मुहूर्तमिव ध्यात्वा दुःखामर्षसमन्विता । भर्तारमभिसंप्रेक्ष्य कुद्धा वचनमब्रवीत् ॥२४॥
verses.english: Collecting her thought in a moment, she thus addressed her husband looking straight at him in grief and in anger. “O great king, knowing everything, how can you, like a mean and inferior man, say that you know nothing'?

verses.sanskrit: जानन्नपि महाराज कस्मादेवं प्रभाषसे। न जानामीति निःशङ्कं यथान्यः प्राकृतो जनः॥२५॥
अत्र ते हृदयं वेद सत्यस्यैवानृतस्य च । कल्याणं वद साक्ष्येण मात्मानमवमन्यथाः ॥२६॥
verses.english: Your heart is the witness to the truth or to the falsehood of my words. Therefore, speak the truth and do not degrade yourself.

verses.sanskrit: योऽन्यथा संतमात्मानमन्यथा प्रतिपद्यते । किं तेन न कृतं पापं चौरेणात्मापहारिणा॥२७॥
verses.english: He, who has one thing in his mind, but represents another thing to others, is a thief and a robber of his own self. What sin is he not capable of committing?

verses.sanskrit: एकोऽहमस्मीति च मन्यसे त्वं न हृच्छयं वेत्सि मुनिं पुराणम् । यो वेदिता कर्मणः पापकस्य तस्यान्तिके त्वं वृजिनं करोषि ॥२८॥
verses.english: You think that you alone know what you did. But do you not know that the great Omniscient One dwells in your heart. He knows all your sins and you sin in his presence.

verses.sanskrit: मन्यते पापकं कृत्वा न कश्चिद्वेत्ति मामिति । विदन्ति चैनं देवाश्च यश्चैवान्तरपूरुषः ॥२९॥
verses.english: Man, when sinning, thinks that no one sees him. But he is seen by the celestials and by the Deity who dwells in every heart.

verses.sanskrit: आदित्यचन्द्रावनिलानलौ च द्यौर्भूमिरापो हृदयं यमश्च । अहश्च रात्रिश्च उभे च संध्ये धर्मश्च जानाति नरस्य वृत्तम् ॥३०॥
verses.english: The sun, the moon, the air, the fire, the earth, the sky, the water, the heart, Yama, the day, the night, the twilight and Dharma see every act of man.

verses.sanskrit: यमो वैवस्वतस्तस्य निर्यातयति दुष्कृतम् । हृदि स्थितः कर्मसाक्षी क्षेत्रज्ञो यस्य तुष्यति॥३१॥
verses.english: Yama, the son of Vivasvata, takes no account of the sins of that man with whom the Deity, the witness of all acts, remains pleased.

verses.sanskrit: न तु तुष्यति यस्यैष पुरुषस्य दुरात्मनः । तं यमः पापकर्माणं वियातयति दुष्कृतम् ॥३२॥
verses.english: But that sinner, with whom the great Deity is not pleased, is punished by Yama for his wicked deeds.

verses.sanskrit: योवमन्यात्मनात्मानमन्यथा प्रतिपद्यते। न तस्य देवाः श्रेयांसो यस्यात्माऽपि न कारणम् ॥३३॥
verses.english: He, who falsely represents his self and thus degrades himself, is never blessed by the celestials. Even his own soul does not bless him. I have come of my own accord, but I am a devoted wife to my husband. Do not disrespect me. I am your wife and deserve to be treated respectfully.
verses.bhavadeepa: वियातयति विशेषेण यातनां पीडां करोति । दुष्कृतं दुष्टं कृतमस्य तम्  ॥३२॥

verses.sanskrit: स्वयं प्राप्तेति मामेवं माऽवमंस्थाः पतिव्रताम् । अर्चार्हां नार्चयसि मां स्वयं भार्यामुपस्थिताम् ॥३४॥
किमर्थं मां प्राकृतवदुपप्रेक्षसि संसदि । न खल्वहमिदं शून्ये रौमि किं न शृणोषि मे॥३५॥
verses.english: Why do you treat me before all these men like an ordinary woman? I am certainly not crying in the wilderness. Do you not hear me?

verses.sanskrit: यदि मे याचमानाया वचनं न करिष्यसि । दुष्यन्त शतधा मूर्धा ततस्तेऽद्य स्फुटिष्यति॥३६॥
verses.english: O Dushyanta, If you refuse what I ask you to do, your head will to day be divided into a thousand pieces.

verses.sanskrit: भार्यां पतिः संप्रविश्य स यस्माज्जायते पुनः । जायायास्तद्धि जायात्वं पौराणाः कवयो विदुः ॥३७॥
verses.english: The learned men of old say that the husband himself, entering into the womb of his wife, comes out as the son. Therefore, the wife is called Jaya.

verses.sanskrit: यदागमवतः पुंसस्तदपत्यं प्रजायते। तत्तारयति संतत्या पूर्वप्रेतान्पितामहान् ॥३८॥
verses.english: The son, that is born to a wise man, rescues the spirits of his deceased ancestors.
verses.bhavadeepa: पौराणाः कवयो वैदिकाः ‘तज्जाया जाया भवति यदस्यां जायते पुनः’ इत्यादि मन्त्रविदः  ॥३७॥

verses.sanskrit: पुंनांम्नो नरकाद्यस्मात्पित्तरं त्रायते सुतः। तस्मात्पुत्र इति प्रोक्तः स्वयमेव स्वयंभुवा ॥३९॥
verses.english: Because the son rescues his ancestors from the hell, called Put, therefore he has been called by the self-created (Brahma) himself as Putra.

verses.sanskrit: सा भार्या या गृहे दक्षा सा भार्या या प्रजावती । सा भार्या या पतिप्राणा सा भार्या या पत्तिव्रता ॥४०॥
verses.english: She is a true wife who is a good housewife; she is a true wife whose heart is devoted to her husband; she is a true wife who is faithful to her husband,
verses.bhavadeepa: पुंनाम्न इत्यन्तः परं ‘पौत्रेण लोकान् जयते पौत्रेणानन्त्यमश्नुते। अथ पौत्रस्य पुत्रेण मोदन्ते प्रपितामहाः’ इति पठन्ति । तत्र पुत्रेण नरकादुद्धतः पौत्रेण स्वर्गे नीयते प्रपौत्रेण ततोप्युपरिनीयते । पुत्रेणैव स्वर्गे नीतः पौत्रेण ब्रह्मलोके प्रापित आनन्त्यं मोक्षं लभते । तेनासौ प्रपौत्रमपेक्षत इत्यर्थः ॥ ३९॥

verses.sanskrit: अर्धं भार्या मनुष्यस्य भार्या श्रेष्ठतमः सखा । भार्या मूलं त्रिवर्गस्य भार्या मूलं तरिष्यतः ॥४१॥
verses.english: A man's half is his wife, the wife is her husband's best of friends; the wife is the source of Dharma, Artha and Kama; the wife is the source of salvation.

verses.sanskrit: भार्यावन्तः क्रियावन्तः सभार्या गृहमेधिनः । भार्यावन्तः प्रमोदन्ते भार्यावन्तः श्रियान्विताः ॥४२॥
verses.english: Those that have wives can perform religious acts; those that have wives lead domestic lives. Those that have wives can be happy and those that have wives can achieve good fortune.

verses.sanskrit: सखायः प्रविविक्तेषु भवन्त्येताः प्रियंवदाः । पितरो धर्मकार्येषु भवन्त्यार्तस्य मातरः ॥४३॥
verses.english: The sweet-speeched wives their husband's friends on the occasion of joy; they are as fathers on occasions of religious acts; they are as mothers in the hours of illness and are woe.

verses.sanskrit: कान्तारेष्वपि विश्रामो जनस्याध्वानकस्य वै । यः सदारः सविश्वास्यस्तस्माद्दाराः परागतिः॥४४॥
verses.english: Even in the deep forest, the wife is the refreshment and solace to her roaming husband. He who has a wife, is trusted by all. The wife, therefore, is man's great means of salvation.

verses.sanskrit: संसरन्तमपि प्रेतं विषमेष्वेकपातिनम् । मार्यैवान्वेति भर्तारं सततं या पतिव्रता ॥४५॥
verses.english: When the husband goes to the land of Yama, leaving this world, it is the devoted wife only that accompanies him there.

verses.sanskrit: प्रथमं संस्थिता भार्या पतिं प्रेत्य प्रतीक्ष्यते । पूर्वं मृतं च भर्तारं पश्चात्साध्व्यनुगच्छति ॥४६॥
verses.english: The wife, gone before (dying before her husband), waits for the spirit of her husband and if the husband goes before, the chaste wife soon follows him.

verses.sanskrit: एतस्मात्कारणाद्राजन्पाणिग्रहणमिष्यते। यदाप्नोति पतिर्मार्यामिहलोके परत्र च ॥४७॥
verses.english: O king, for all these reasons, marriage exists (in this world). The husband enjoys the company of his wife, both here in this world and hereafter.

verses.sanskrit: आत्मात्मनैव जनितः पुत्र इत्युच्यते बुधैः । तस्माद्भार्थी नरः पश्येन्मातृवत्पुत्रमातरम् ॥४८॥
verses.english: The learned men have said that a man himself is born as his son; therefore, a man whose wife has given birth to a son, should look upon her as his mother.

verses.sanskrit: भार्यायां जनितं पुत्रमादर्शेष्विव चाननम् । ह्लादते जनिता प्रेक्ष्य स्वर्गं प्राप्येव पुण्यकृत् ॥४९॥
verses.english: Looking at the face of the son, begotten on his wife, a man sees his own face as he does in a mirror; and feels himself as happy as a virtuous man attaining to heaven.

verses.sanskrit: दह्यमाना मनोदुःखैर्व्याधिभिश्चातुरा नराः । ह्लादन्ते स्वेषु दारेषु घर्मार्ताः सलिलेष्विव ॥५०॥
verses.english: Men, burnt out by mental grief or afflicted by disease, feel as much relieved in the company of their wives as a perspiring man does in a cool bath.

verses.sanskrit: सुसंरब्धोऽपि रामाणां न कुर्यादप्रियं नरः। रातं प्रीतिं च धर्मं च तास्वायत्तमवेक्ष्य हि ॥५१॥
verses.english: No man, even in anger, should even do any thing that is disagreeable to his wife; for happiness, joy, virtue and everything depend on the wife.

verses.sanskrit: आत्मनो जन्मनः क्षेत्रं पुण्यं रामाः सनातनम् । ऋषीणामपि का शक्तिः स्रष्टुं रामामृते प्रजाम्॥५२॥
verses.english: Wife is the sacred soil in which the husband is born again. Even Rishis cannot create men without women.

verses.sanskrit: प्रतिपद्य यदा सूनुर्धरणी रेणुगुण्ठितः । पितुराश्लिष्यतेऽङ्गानि किमस्त्यभ्यधिकं ततः॥५३॥
verses.english: What is a greater happiness to a father than what the father feels when his son, running to him, clasps him with his (tiny little) arms, though his body is full of dust and dirt?

verses.sanskrit: स त्वं स्वयमभिप्राप्तं साभिलाषमिमं सुतम् । प्रेक्षमाणं कटाक्षेण किमर्थमवमन्यसे॥५४॥
verses.english: Why are you treating with indifference this your son who has himself come to you and who is wistfully casting his glances towards you? Even ants support their off-spring and do not destroy their eggs. Why then should you not, being learned in the rules of piety, support your own child?

verses.sanskrit: अण्डानि बिभ्रति स्वानि न भिन्दति पिपीलिकाः । न भरेथाः कथं नु त्वं धर्मशः सन्खमात्मजम् ॥५५॥
न वाससां न रामाणां नापां स्पर्शस्तथाविधः। शिशोरालिङ्ग्यमानस्य स्पर्शः सूनोर्यथा सुखः॥५६॥
verses.english: The touch of the sandal-paste, that of women and water, is not so pleasing as that of one's own infant son, locked in his embrace.

verses.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणो द्विपदां श्रेष्ठो गौर्बरिष्ठा चतुष्पदाम्। गुरुर्गरीयसां श्रेष्ठः पुत्रः स्पर्शवतां वरः ॥५७॥
verses.english: As the Brahmana is the best among bipeds (men), as cow is the best among quadrupeds, as preceptor is the best among all superiors, so is the son among all objects pleasing to the touch.

verses.sanskrit: स्पृशतु त्वां समाश्लिष्य पुत्रोऽयं प्रियदर्शनः। पुत्रस्पर्शात्सुखतरः स्पर्शो लोके न विद्यते॥५८॥
verses.english: Let this handsome son touch you in your embrace. There is nothing in the world more pleasing to the touch than that of a son.

verses.sanskrit: त्रिषु वर्षेषु पूर्णेषु प्रजाताऽहमरिंदम् । इमं कुमारं राजेन्द्र तव शोकविनाशनम् ॥५९॥
verses.english: O chastiser of foes, O great king, I gave birth to this boy, the dispeller of your grief, after the completion of three years. O descendant of the Puru race, when I was in the lying-in room, the following words were uttered in the sky, He shall perform one hundred horse-sacrifices.

verses.sanskrit: आहर्ता वाजिमेधस्य शतसंख्यस्य पौरव। इति वागन्तरिक्षे मां सूतकेऽभ्यवदत्पुरा ॥६०॥
ननु नामाङ्कमारोप्य स्नेहाद्ग्रामान्तरं गताः । मूर्ध्नि पुत्रानुपाघ्राय प्रतिनन्दन्ति मानवाः ॥६१॥
verses.english: Men, going to places remote from their homes, take up other men's sons on their laps and smelling their heads, feel great happiness.

verses.sanskrit: वेदेष्वपि वदन्तीमं मन्त्रग्रामं द्विजातयः । जातकर्मणि पुत्राणां तवापि विदितं तथा ॥६२॥
verses.english: You know that the Brahmanas utter the following Vedic Mantras at the birthday, ceremony of the child.

verses.sanskrit: अङ्गादङ्गात्संभवसि हृदया‌दधिजायसे । आत्मा वै पुत्र नामासि स जीव शरदः शतम्॥६३॥
verses.english: “You are born of my body; you have sprung from my heart. You are myself in the form of my son. Live for one hundred years."

verses.sanskrit: जीवितं त्वदधीनं मे संतानमपि चाक्षयम् । तस्मात्वं जीव मे पुत्र सुसुखी शरदां शलम् ॥६४॥
verses.english: "My life depends on you. The continuation of my race also depends on you. Therefore, live in happiness for one hundred years."

verses.sanskrit: त्वदङ्गेभ्यः प्रसुतोऽयं पुरुषात्पुरुषोपरः। सरसीवामलेत्मानं द्वितीयं पश्य वै सुतम् ॥६५॥
verses.english: He (this boy) has sprung from your body, he is a second being begotten from you. Behold your own self in your own son, as you see your image in the clear waters of the lake.

verses.sanskrit: यथा ह्याहवनीयोऽग्निर्गार्हपत्यात्मणीयते। तथा त्वत्तः प्रसूतोऽयं त्वमेकः सन्द्विधाकृतः॥६६॥
verses.english: As the sacrificial fire is kindled from the domestic fire, so has this one (your son), sprung from you. Though you are one, you have divided yourself in two. O king, in your hunting expedition, I was approached by you when I was a virgin in my father's hermitage.
verses.bhavadeepa: त्मानम् आत्मानं द्वितीयम् । प्रतिबिम्बे इव तव सादृश्यमत्र पश्येति भावः  ॥६५॥

verses.sanskrit: मृगावकृष्टेन पुरा मृगयां परिधावताः। अहमासादिता राजन्कुमारी पितुराथमे ॥६७॥
verses.bhavadeepa: एकः सन्पुत्रे जाते योगीवद्द्विधाकृतो द्वैरूप्यं गतः  ॥६६॥

verses.sanskrit: उर्वशीपूर्वचित्तिश्च सहजन्या च मेनका । विश्वाची च घृताची च षडेवाप्सरसां वराः॥६८॥
verses.english: Urvashi, Purvachitti, Sahajanya, Menaka, Vishvachi and Ghritachi, these are the six foremost Apsaras.

verses.sanskrit: तासां सा मेनका नाम ब्रह्मयोनिर्वराप्सराः। दिवः संप्राप्य जगतीं विश्वामित्रादजीजनत्॥६९॥
verses.english: Amongst them again, Menaka, born of a Brahmana, is the first. Descending from heaven on earth, she gave me birth from her association with Vishvamitra.

verses.sanskrit: सा मां हिमवतः प्रस्थे सुषुवे मेनकाऽप्सराः। अवकीर्य च मां यातां परात्मजमिवासती॥७०॥
verses.english: The Apsara Menaka gave me birth in a valley of the Himalayas. Devoid of affections, she went away, leaving me there, as if I was a child of some others.

verses.sanskrit: किं नु कर्मांशुभं पूर्व कृतवत्यन्यजन्मनि। यदहं बान्धवैस्त्यक्ता बाल्ये संप्रति च त्वया ॥७१॥
verses.english: What great sin did I commit of old in some other life that I was cast away by my parents in my infancy and now I am cast away by you?

verses.sanskrit: कामं त्वया परित्यक्ता गमिष्यामि स्वमाश्रमम् । इमं तु बालं संत्यक्तुं नार्हस्यात्मजमात्मनः॥७२॥
verses.english: Cast off from you, I am ready to go back to the hermitage. But you should not cast off this child who is your own son.

verses.sanskrit:
दुष्यन्त उवाच ।
              न पुत्रमभिजानामि त्वयि जातं शकुन्तले । असत्यवचना नार्यः कस्ते श्रद्धास्यते वचः ॥७३॥
verses.english: Dushyanta said : O Shakuntala, I do not know that I begot this child on you. Women generally speak falsehood. Who will believe your words? Your mother is lewd Menaka, destitute of affection; she cast off you in the valley of the Himalayas as one casts off the flowers after offering them to the gods.

verses.sanskrit: मेनका निरनुक्रोशा बन्धकी जननी तव । यया हिमवतः पृष्ठे निर्माल्यमिव चोज्झिता ॥७४॥
स चापि निरनुक्रोशः क्षत्रयोनिः पिता तव । विश्वामित्रो ब्राह्मणत्वे लुब्धः कामवशं गतः॥७५॥
verses.english: Your father also is lustful Vishvamitra of the Kshatriya race, destitute of all affection, the ! man who was tempted to become a Brahmana.

verses.sanskrit: मेनकाऽप्सरसां श्रेष्ठा महर्षीणां पिता च ते । तयोरपत्यं कस्मात्त्वं पुंश्चलीव प्रमाषसे ॥७६॥
verses.english: But (if you say), Menaka is the foremost of Apsaras and Vishvamitra is the foremost of Rishis, why then do you, being their daughter, speak like a lewd woman?
verses.bhavadeepa: तव पितरौ नीचौ उच्चैौ चेत्कथं त्वमेवं भाषस इत्याह द्वाभ्यां स चेति  ॥७५॥

verses.sanskrit: अश्रद्धेयमिदं वाक्यं कथयन्ती न लज्जसे । विशेषतो मत्सकाशे दुष्टतापसि गम्यताम् ॥७७॥
verses.english: Your these words deserve no credence. Are you not ashamed to utter them, specially before me? Go away, O wicked ascetic woman.

verses.sanskrit: क्व महर्षिः स चैवाग्र्यः साऽप्सरा क्व च मेनका। क्व च त्वमेवं कृपणा तापसी वेषधारिणी ॥७८॥
verses.english: Where is now that best of great Rishis (Vishvamitra) and that best of Apsaras Menaka? And where are you, (though) in the humble garb of ascetics.

verses.sanskrit: अतिकायश्च ते पुत्रो बालोऽतिबलवानयम्। कथमल्पेन कालेन शालस्तम्भ इवोद्गतः॥७९॥
verses.english: Your this son is very big and appears to be very strong. How has he, within so short time, grown up like a Sala sprout?

verses.sanskrit: सुनिकृष्टा च ते योनिः पुंश्चलीष प्रभाषसे । यदृच्छया कामरागाज्जाता मेनकया ह्यसि ॥८०॥
verses.english: You are born very low, you speak also like a lewd woman. You were lustfully conceived by Menaka.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वमेतत्परोक्षं मे यत्त्वं वद्धि तापसि । नाहं त्वामभिजानामि यथेष्टं गम्यतां त्वया ॥८१॥
verses.english: O ascetic woman, all that you say is quite unknown to me. I do not know you. Go away wherever you please.

verses.sanskrit: शकुन्तलोवाच । राजन्सर्षपमात्राणि परच्छिद्राणि पश्यसि। आत्मनो बिल्वमात्राणि पश्यन्नपि न पश्यसि ॥८२॥
verses.english: Shakuntala said: O king, you (can) see the faults of others, though they may be as small as the mustard seed. But you can not see your own faults, though they are as big as the Bilva fruit.

verses.sanskrit: मेनका त्रिदशेष्वेव त्रिदशाश्चानुमेनकाम्। ममैवोद्रिच्यते जन्म दुष्यन्त तव जन्मनः ॥८३॥
verses.english: Menaka is a celestial, (nay) Menaka is considered to be the best of celestial. O Dushyanta, my birth is noble than your own.

verses.sanskrit: क्षितावटसि राजेन्द्र अन्तरिक्षे चराम्यहम्। आवयोरन्तरं पश्य मेरुसर्षपयोरिव ॥८४॥
verses.english: O great king, you walk on earth, but I roam in the sky. Know that the difference between you and me is like that of a mustard seed and the Meru (mountain).

verses.sanskrit: महेन्द्रस्य कुबेरस्य यमस्य वरुणस्य च । भवनान्यनुसंयामि प्रभावं पश्य मे नृप ॥८५॥
verses.english: O king, behold, I can go to the abodes of Indra, Kubera, Yama and Varuna.

verses.sanskrit: सत्यश्चापि प्रवादोयं यं प्रवक्ष्यामि तेऽनघ। निदर्शनार्थं न द्वेषाच्छ्रुत्वा तं क्षन्तुमर्हसि॥८६॥
verses.english: O sinless man, there is a proverb which I am going to mention to you; (but I am not doing it) from any evil motive, but only as an example. Therefore, kindly pardon me for referring to it.

verses.sanskrit: विरूपो यावदादर्शे नात्मनः पश्यते मुखम् । मन्यते तावदात्मानमन्येभ्यो रूपवत्तरम् ॥८७॥
verses.english: The ugly man, until he sees his face in a mirror, considers himself more handsome than others.

verses.sanskrit: यदा स्वमुखमादर्शे विकृतं सोऽभिवीक्षते। तदान्तरं विजानीते आत्मानं चेतरं जनम्॥८८॥
verses.english: But when he sees his own face in the mirror, it is then that he perceives the difference between himself and others.

verses.sanskrit: अतीवरूपसंपन्नो न कंचिदवमन्यते । अतीवजल्पन्दुर्वाचो भवतीह विहेठकः ॥८९॥
verses.english: He, who is really very handsome, never taunts others. He, who too much vilifies others, is only considered to be a reviler.

verses.sanskrit: मूर्खो हि जल्पतां पुंसां श्रुत्वा वाचः शुभाशुभाः। अशुभं वाक्यमादत्ते पुरीषमिव सूकरः॥९०॥
verses.english: As the swine seeks for the dirt and filth even when it is in a flower-garden, so does a wicked man chose only evil out of the evil and the good that others speak.

verses.sanskrit: प्राज्ञस्तु जल्पतां पुंसां श्रुत्वा वाचः शुभाशुभाः। गुणवद्वाक्यमादते हंसः क्षीरमिवाम्भसः॥९१॥
verses.english: But as the geese always extract milk, though inixed with water, so does a wise man accept only what is good from the speech that is intermixed with both good and evil.

verses.sanskrit: अन्यान्परिवदन्साधुर्यथा हि परितप्यते । तथा परिवदन्नन्यांस्तुष्टो भवति दुर्जनः ॥९२॥
verses.english: Honest men always feel pain to speak ill of others, but wicked men always derive pleasure in doing it.

verses.sanskrit: अभिवाद्य यथा वृद्धान्सन्तो गच्छन्ति निर्वृतिम् । एवं सज्जनमाक्रुक्ष्य मूर्खा भवति निर्वृतः॥९३॥
verses.english: Honest men always feel pleasure in showing respect towards the old (good men), but the fools always feel pleasure in abusing them. Honest men are happy in not seeking others' fault, but the fools are happy in doing it. The wicked always speak ill of honest men, but honest men never injure the wicked, even if injured by them.

verses.sanskrit: सुखं जीवन्त्यदोषज्ञा मूर्खा दोषानुदर्शिनः । यत्र वाच्याः परैः सन्तः परानाहुस्तथाविधान्॥९४॥
अतो हास्यतरं लोके किंचिदन्यन्न विद्यते । यत्र दुर्जनमित्याह दुर्जनः सज्जनं स्वयम् ॥९५॥
verses.english: What could be more ridiculous in the world than this, that those that are wicked should represent really honest men as wicked.
verses.bhavadeepa: यत्र विषये परैः सद्भिः वाच्याः निन्द्याः सन्तो दुरात्मानः परान्साधून्निन्द्यानाहुः ॥९४॥

verses.sanskrit: सत्यधर्मच्युतात्पुंसः क्रुद्धादाशीविषादिव। अनास्तिकोऽप्युद्विजते जनः किं पुनरास्तिकः॥९६॥
verses.english: Even atheists are afraid of those who have fallen from truth and virtue, as all men are afraid of the snakes of virulent poison. (When such is the case with an atheist), what shall I speak of me who is atheist?

verses.sanskrit: स्वयमुत्पाद्य वै पुत्रं सदृशं यो न मन्यते । तस्य देवाः श्रियं घ्नन्ति न च लोकानुपाश्नुते ॥९७॥
verses.english: The man, who having begotten a son who is his own image, does not look after him, never gains the higher worlds. The celestial destroy his good fortune an wealth.

verses.sanskrit: कुलवंशप्रतिष्ठां हि पितरः पुत्रमब्रुवन् । उत्तमं सर्वधर्माणां तस्मात्पुत्रं न संत्यजेत् ॥९८॥
verses.english: The Pitris (ancestors) have said that the son continues the race and supports the relations; therefore, to give birth to a son is the best of all pious acts. Therefore, your this son should not be abandoned.

verses.sanskrit: स्वपत्नीप्रभवान्पञ्च लब्धान्कीतान्विवार्धितान् । कृतानन्यासु चोत्पन्नान्पुत्रान्वै मनुरब्रवीत् ॥९९॥
verses.english: Manu has said that there are five kinds of sons, namely those begotten by one on his wife, those obtained from others, those purchased for a price, those reared out of affection and those begotten on other women.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मकीर्त्यावहानॄणां मनसः प्रीतिवर्धनाः। त्रायन्ते नरकाज्जाताः पुत्रा धर्मप्लवाः पितॄन्॥१००॥
verses.english: Sons support the religion and achievements of men; they increase their happiness; they rescue the dead ancestor from hell.
verses.bhavadeepa: स्वपत्नीप्रभवान् अन्यासु चोत्पन्नांश्चतुर्विधानेवं पञ्च पुत्रान्प्रचक्षते । कृतान् उपनयनादिना संस्कृतान्  ॥९९॥

verses.sanskrit: स त्वं नृपतिशार्दूल पुत्रं न त्यक्तुमर्हसि । आत्मानं सत्यधर्मौ च पालयन्पृथिवीपते । नरेन्द्रसिंहकपटं न वोढुं त्वमिहार्हसि॥१०१॥
verses.english: Therefore, O best of kings, it is not proper for you to abandon your son. O king of the earth, cherish your own self, truth and virtue, more more (by cherishing your this son). () best of the kings, it is not proper for you to play hypocrite's in this matter.

verses.sanskrit: वरं कूपशताद्वापी वरं वापीशतात्क्रतुः । वरं ऋतुशतात्पुत्रः सत्यं पुत्रशताद्वरम् ॥१०२॥
verses.english: The dedication of a tank is meritorious than that of one hundred wells. A sacrifice is meritorious than the dedication of a tank. But (to beget a son) is inore meritorious than the celebration of sacrifices. Truth (however) is more meritorious than the birth of one hundred sons.

verses.sanskrit: अश्वमेधसहस्रं च सत्यं च तुलया धृतम् । अश्वमेधसहस्त्राद्धि सत्यमेव विशिष्यते ॥१०३॥
verses.english: If one thousand horse-sacrifices and truth were weighed, truth would be found heavier than one thousand horse-sacrifices.

verses.sanskrit: सर्ववेदाधिगमनं सर्वेतीर्थावगाहनम् । सत्यं च वचनं राजन्समं वा स्यान्न वा समम्॥१०४॥
verses.english: O king, I tell you, truth is equal to the study of the entire Vedas and ablutions in all the sacred pilgrimages.

verses.sanskrit: नास्ति सत्यसमो धर्मो न सत्याद्विद्यते परम् । न हि तीव्रतरं किंचिदनृतादिह विद्यते ॥१०५॥
verses.english: There is no virtue equal to truth, there is nothing (in this world) superior to truth. And there is nothing (again) more sinful than falsehood.

verses.sanskrit: राजन्सत्यं परं ब्रह्म सत्यं च समयः परः । मा त्याक्षीः समयं राजन्सत्यं संगतमस्तु ते ॥१०६॥
verses.english: O king, truth is the great Brahma, truth is the great vow; therefore, O king, do not violate your pledge. Let truth and yourself be ever united.

verses.sanskrit: अनृते चेत्प्रसङ्गस्ते श्रद्दधासि न चेत्स्वयम् । आत्मना हन्त गच्छामि त्वादृशेनास्ति संगतम्॥१०७॥
verses.english: If, however, you are united with falsehood, li you do not place any credence on my word, I shall go away from this place of my own accord. Your companionship should not be sought after.

verses.sanskrit: त्वामृतेऽपि हि दुष्यन्त शैलराजावतंसकाम्। चतुरंतामिमामुर्वीं पुत्रो मे पालयिष्यति ॥१०८॥
verses.english: But, ( Dushyanta, (know this for a certainty), that when you are dead, my this son shall rule the whole earth, surrounded by the four seas and adorned by the king of mountains.

verses.sanskrit:
वैशंपायन उवाच ।
              एतावदुक्त्वा राजानं प्रातिष्ठत शकुन्तला । अथान्तरिक्षाद्दुष्यन्तं वागुवाचाशरीरिणी ॥१०९॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said : Having said all this to the king, Shakuntala turned her back. Thereupon a voice from the sky, coming from one who had no visible shape, addressed Dushyanta who was sitting, surrounded by his ministers, priests and Ritvikas.
verses.bhavadeepa: अत्र ‘ऋतेऽपि गर्दभक्षीरात्पयः पास्यति मे सुतः’ इति क्वचित्पठ्यते तस्यायं भावः । गर्दभी क्षीवत्त्वया दत्तमपि राज्यं परित्यज्य स्वभुजबलेनैव मत्पुत्रो राज्यं करिष्यतीति । त्वामिति चतुरन्तां चतुःसमुद्रान्ताम्  ॥१०८॥

verses.sanskrit: ऋत्विक्पुरोहिताचार्यैर्मन्त्रिभिश्च वृतं तदा । भस्त्रा माता पितुः पुत्रो येन जातः स एव सः॥११०॥
verses.english: (It said), “O Dushyanta, the mother is but a sheath of flesh (within which the son dwells). The son, sprung from the father, is the father himself. Therefore, cherish your son and do not insult Shakuntala. O best of men, the son begotten by one's own self, rescues him from the abode of Yama. You are the father of this son. Shakuntala has spoken the truth. The husband divides his body in two parts and is born in the womb of his wife as the son.

verses.sanskrit: भरस्व पुत्रं दुष्यन्त मावमंस्थाः शकुन्तलाम् । रेतोधाः पुत्र उन्नयति नरदेवयमक्षयात् ॥१११॥
verses.bhavadeepa: भस्त्रा चर्मकोशः । तत्र निहितं बीजं यथा तदीयं न भवति एवं मातापि भस्त्रेव । येन हेतुना यो जातः स एव सः । कार्यस्य कारणानन्यत्वात्  ॥११०॥

verses.sanskrit: त्वं चास्य धाता गर्भस्य सत्यमाह शकुन्तला । जाया जनयते पुत्रमात्मनोऽङ्गाद्द्विधा कृतम् ॥११२॥
verses.bhavadeepa: भरस्व धारयस्व पोषयस्व वा । रेतोधाः रेतः सेक्ता यः स एव पुत्रः पितुरनन्य एवेत्यर्थः । उन्नयति ऊर्ध्वं नयति । यमक्षयात् नरकात् पितॄनिति शेषः  ॥१११॥

verses.sanskrit: तस्माद्भरस्व दुष्यन्त पुत्रं शाकुन्तलं नृप । अभूतिरेषा यत्त्यक्त्वा जीवेज्जिवन्तमात्मजम्॥११३॥
verses.english: O king, O Dushyanta, therefore, cherish your this son, born of Shakuntala. To forsake one's own son and to live thereafter is a great misfortune.

verses.sanskrit: शाकुन्तलं महात्मानं दौष्यन्तिं भर पौरव । भर्तव्योऽयं त्वया यस्मादस्माकं वचनादपि ॥११४॥
verses.english: Therefore, O descendant of the Puru race, cherish your this high-souled son, born of Shakuntala. As you will cherish this child at our word, therefore, your this son will be known by the name of Bharata.

verses.sanskrit: तस्माद्भवत्वयं नाम्ना भरतो नाम ते सुतः । तच्छ्रुत्वा पौरवो राजा व्याहृतं त्रिदिवौकसाम्॥११५॥
verses.english: Having heard these words of the dwellers of heaven, the king of the Puru race was much pleased and addressing his priests and ministers, he said : “Hear all of you the words of the messenger of heaven."

verses.sanskrit: पुरोहितममात्यांश्च संप्रहृष्टोऽब्रवीदिदम् । शृण्वन्त्वेतद्भवन्तोऽस्य देवदूतस्य भाषितम् ॥११६॥
अहं चाप्येवमेवैनं जानामि स्वयमात्मजम् । भवेद्धि शङ्क्यो लोकस्य नैव शुद्धो भवेदयम् ॥११७॥
verses.english: "I myself know that this boy is my son. If I had accepted him as my son at Shakuntala's words, my people would have been suspicious and my son also would not have been considered to be pure (of pure birth).”

verses.sanskrit: वैशंपायन उवाच । तं विशोध्य तदा राजा देवदूतेन भारत । हृष्टः प्रमुदितञ्चापि प्रतिजग्राह तं सुतम् ॥११८॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said : O descendant of the Virata race, the king was exceedingly pleased, because the purity of the birth of his son was established by the messenger of heaven.

verses.sanskrit: ततस्तस्य तदा राजा पितृकर्माणि सर्वशः । कारयामास मुदितः प्रीतिमानात्मजस्य ह ॥११९॥
verses.english: He then performed with joy all those rites which a father should perform for his son.

verses.sanskrit: मूर्ध्नि चैनमुपाघ्राय सस्नेहं परिषस्वजे । सभाज्यमानो विप्रैश्च स्तूयमानश्च वन्दिभिः । स मुदं परमां लेभे पुत्रसंस्पर्शजां नृपः ॥१२०॥
verses.english: He smelt his son's head; he embraced him with affection. The Brahmanas uttered blessings on him and the bards began to applaud him. The king then enjoyed the great pleasure that one feels at the touch of one's own son.

verses.sanskrit: तां चैव भार्यां दुष्यन्तः पूजयामास धर्मतः । अब्रवीच्चैव तां राजा सान्त्वपूर्वमिदं वचः ॥१२१॥
verses.english: Dushyanta also received his wife (Shakuntala) with all honour and affection. Affectionately pacifying her, he spoke to her thus,

verses.sanskrit: कृतो लोकपरोक्षोऽयं संबन्धोऽयं त्वया सह । तस्मादेतन्मया देवि त्वष्छुद्ध्यर्थं विचारितम् ॥१२२॥
verses.english: “O lady, my union with you took place in private. None knew of it and therefore, it is natural that people should have thought that our union was only out of lust and that we were not husband and wife. This son, installed as my heir-apparent, would have been considered as a man of impure birth. Therefore, I was thinking how best to establish your purity.

verses.sanskrit: मन्यते चैव लोकास्ते स्त्रीभावान्मथि संगतम् । पुत्रश्चायं वृतो राज्ये मया तस्माद्विचारितम्॥१२३॥
यच्च कोपितयात्यर्थं त्वयोक्तोऽस्म्यप्रियं प्रिये। प्रणयिन्या विशालाक्षि तत्क्षान्तं ते मया शुभे॥१२४॥
verses.english: "O dearest, O lady of beautiful eyes, I have forgiven you for all the hard words you have uttered in anger. You are my darling.”

verses.sanskrit: तामेवमुक्त्वा राजर्षिर्दुष्यन्तो महिषीं प्रियाम् । वासोभिरन्नपानैश्च पूजयामास भारत ॥१२५॥
verses.english: O descendant of the Bharata race, having spoken thus to his dear queen (Shakuntala), the royal sage Dushyanta, received her with the presents of perfume, food and drink.

verses.sanskrit: दुष्यन्तस्तु तदा राजा पुत्रं शाकुन्तलं तदा । भरतं नामतः कृत्वा यौवराज्येऽभ्यषेचयत् ॥१२६॥
तस्य तत्प्रथितं चक्रं प्रावर्तत महात्मनः। भास्वरं दिव्यमजितं लोकसंनादनं महत् ॥१२७॥
verses.english: From that day the invincible car of Bharata, like the car of the celestials, with its famous and bright wheels, traversed the whole earth, filling it with its rattle.

verses.sanskrit: स विजित्य महीपालांश्चकार वशवर्तिनः । चचार च सतां धर्मं प्राप चानुत्तमं यशः ॥१२८॥
verses.english: The son of Dushyanta (Bharata) brought under his sway all the kings of the world. He ruled his subjects virtuously and gained great fame.

verses.sanskrit: स राजा चक्रवर्त्यासीत्सार्वभौमः प्रतापवान्। ईजे च बहुभिर्यज्ञैर्यथा शक्रो मरुत्पतिः ॥१२९॥
verses.english: That king (Bharata) was known by the name of Chakravarti and Sarvabhauma. He performed many sacrifices like Indra, the lord of the Marutas.

verses.sanskrit: याजयामास तं कण्वो विधिवद्भूरिदक्षिणम् । श्रीमान्गोविततं नाम वाजिमेधमवाप सः । यस्मिन्सहस्रं पद्मानां कण्वाय भरतो ददौ ॥१३०॥
verses.english: Kanva was the chief priest in those sacrifices and great offerings were made to the Brahmanas. The fortunate king performed both the cow and the horse-sacrifices. Bharata gave one thousand gold coins to Kanva as his sacrificial fee.
verses.bhavadeepa: चक्रं रथचक्रम् आज्ञा वा अन्यतरेण सर्वं व्याप्नोतीति चक्रवर्ती । सार्वभौमः सर्वभूमीश्वरः  ॥१२९॥

verses.sanskrit: भरताद्भारती कीर्तिर्येनेदं भारतं कुलम् । अपरे ये च पूर्वे वै भारता इति विश्रुताः ॥१३१॥
verses.english: From this Bharata has followed this, "achievement of Bharata," from him has sprung this great race (of Bharata.) All kings that were born after him are called after his name.

verses.sanskrit: भरतस्यान्ववाये हि देवकल्पा महौजसः। बभूवुर्ब्रह्मकल्पाश्च वहवो राजसत्तमाः॥१३२॥
verses.english: And in this Bharata race were many godlike and greatly powerful best of monarchs. They were like Brahma himself. Their names are countless. O descendant of the Bharata race, I shall name only the chief ones, who were all blessed with great fortune and devoted to truth and honesty. They were all like the celestial.

verses.sanskrit: येषामपरिमेयानि नामधेयानि सर्वशः । तेषां तु ते यथामुख्यं कीर्तयिष्यामि भारत। महाभागान्देवकल्पान्सत्यार्जवपरायणान्॥१३३॥
